samples.summary: Third divergent implementation of "where does the cursor go when the current slide disappears". `resolveCurrentSlide` clamps to `currentIndex - 1` (backwards), while `presenter.ts:573` clamps to the OLD index (i.e. forward, onto the slide that took its place), `thumbnail-panel.ts:315-318` prefers the first surviving slide AFTER the anchor, and `mobile-slides-view.tsx:188-190` falls back to `slideIds[0]`. Same event (a peer deleting the slide you are on) now moves the cursor backwards in the editor and forwards in the presenter. The rule is small enough to live once in `packages/slides/src/model/` and be reused by all three, which is the reuse posture this repo states; instead the diff adds a fourth behaviour. Acceptance criterion "somewhere valid" is still met, so this is consistency/reuse, not a spec failure.

No design doc records the new editor invariant ("currentId is revalidated at the resolution point; the editor carries a `currentIndex` shadow of the cursor"). `docs/design/slides/slides.md` has no current-slide/cursor section, and `slides-native-undo.md:243-246` explicitly states post-undo cursor/selection reconciliation is "handled by the view layer … No store change required; called out as a smoke-test item" — that is the canonical doc paragraph this change makes concrete, and it was not updated to say where the healing now lives or which rule it uses. Only task/lessons files under docs/tasks/active carry the reasoning, which are not the design record. Arguably a bug fix needs no doc update (CONTRIBUTING.md:13 requires one for "feature / non-trivial change"), hence low confidence.

The resolve point heals a *dangling* cursor but deliberately leaves an *unset* cursor unhealed (`if (id === undefined) return undefined`), so a deck that gains slides after mounting with none still paints nothing. That is the same class of blank-canvas bug as #883 and the same one-line site could cover it; today it is held off only by the convention that `slides-view.tsx:644` seeds a slide before mounting (see the comment there at :634-638). Outside the issue's acceptance criteria, so scope-choice rather than a failed criterion.

Layer choice: the heal mutates cursor state, tears down crop/text-edit/selection and fans out `currentSlideListeners` from inside two paint functions, so `getCurrentSlideId()` keeps returning a removed id for every consumer that reads it before the next paint (frontend toolbar/format-panel/notes-panel all read it on the store-change tick). The repo's precedent for exactly this healing is `presenter.ts:531-583`, which does it in the store-change handler rather than in `paint()`. Desktop happens to call `editor.render()` synchronously inside `store.onChange` (slides-view.tsx:1051-1053), which is why this mostly works, so confidence is low — but the invariant is now guaranteed only for hosts that render promptly, and a host that renders on a throttled RAF exposes the dangling id.
